articles.title: Taiwanese firms waiting to see US commitment before betting on Pax Silica
articles.summary: Taiwanese businesses are taking a "wait-and-see" stance on the proposed Pax Silica hub in New Clark City until Washington signs agreements for the project, a Taiwanese business leader said, amid…

blocks.text: November 26, 2026 | 6:46am

MANILA, Philippines — Taiwanese businesses are taking a "wait-and-see" stance on the proposed Pax Silica hub in New Clark City until Washington signs agreements for the project, a Taiwanese business leader said, amid signs the US is in no hurry to finalize the deal.

Best Chang, president of the Subic Bay Taiwan Chamber of Commerce, said most of the Taiwanese businesses he has spoken with have shown some interest in the hub but first want to see whether the US will finalize the agreements and deliver on its commitments before they invest.
That follow-through from the US, Chang told Philstar.com in an emailed interview on Wednesday, November 25, will strongly influence investor confidence and the timing of investment decisions.

"For Pax Silica to move from plans to actual investment in the Philippines, the United States needs to follow through with signed agreements for the proposed hub, concrete commitments, and implementation," Chang said. "Without that, even the most detailed supporting plans risk remaining plans on paper."
US President Donald Trump's visit to Manila last week came and went without the signing of the agreement that would finalize the Pax Silica industrial hub in New Clark City.
The Bases Conversion and Development Authority, which is developing the 1,620-hectare site, had previously targeted a November signing.
Not a done deal

The US-led Pax Silica initiative aims to secure supply chains for computer chips, artificial intelligence and critical minerals to reduce dependency on China. The Philippines joined in April and offered 1,620 hectares in New Clark City, in Capas, Tarlac, for an advanced manufacturing hub, the first physical site planned under the initiative.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said over the weekend that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had assured him Washington was not rushing the initiative and recognized that Manila first needed to address domestic concerns on the planned hub.

The proposed hub — generally promoted by the Philippine government as a rare opportunity to deliver billions in investments — is facing stiff resistance from a wide range of groups who believe its projected benefits do not outweigh the damage it may bring to communities and the environment.

Critics, led by Indigenous groups, farmers, and progressive coalitions, remain unconvinced by official assurances of the hub's impact on local communities. Several groups, including rights watchdog Human Rights Watch, have warned that the Pax Silica project will displace residents, siphon off scarce water supplies, and overburden the Luzon power grid.

Taiwan has not signed the Pax Silica declaration but takes part as a non-signatory participant. It was the largest source of foreign investment approved in the Philippines in the third quarter, accounting for P76.27 billion, or nearly half of the total, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority.
Finance Secretary Frederick Go said in July that Foxconn, a Taiwanese electronics manufacturer, was poised to become the hub's anchor locator, or main tenant.

Chang said a delegation from the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association, which came to the Philippines in late July to look at investment opportunities, showed interest within Taiwanese industry.
"However, interest, site visits, and firm investment commitments are different stages and should not be confused," he said.

Once US commitments are in place, Chang said, companies would weigh conditions at the site itself, including the supply and cost of power, the availability of workers, transport and logistics, and how clear and predictable regulations, incentives and procedures are.
"Both US follow-through and the Philippines' readiness to support investors are essential to turning interest into actual investment," he said.
Taiwanese investments in the PH
Chang said he was "cautiously optimistic" about more Taiwanese investment in the Philippines.

His chamber, founded in 1998 by Taiwanese manufacturers in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, joined Taiwan Association, Inc. as its Subic Bay chapter on November 21, a move he said was meant "to turn closer cooperation into tangible benefits for our members, rather than simply change the organizational structure."
BCDA vice president Erwin Kenneth Peralta told Taiwan's Central News Agency (CNA) on November 21 that the New Clark City park was still at the framework planning stage, according to a report.
Full development of the site would take 20 to 25 years, with the first five years spent on land preparation, roads and utility lines before factories are built.
Peralta was briefing more than 30 Taiwanese businesspeople who visited New Clark City that day on a trip organized by Taiwan Association, Inc., CNA reported.

He said the government was trying to attract Taiwanese companies to the park and that two of the three major international companies already in New Clark City are Taiwanese. Chang did not join the trip, saying he visits the area once or twice a year.
Steve Chien, a vice president of Taiwan Association, Inc., told CNA that electricity and water are relatively expensive in the Philippines.
He said New Clark City's power demand is projected to reach 2,000 megawatts, while nearly 200 megawatts, about a tenth of that, is available so far.

articles.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie settle years-long legal battle over joint French winery
articles.summary:
Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in 2022 after she sold her stake in Château Miraval, saying she broke their agreement not to sell their interests

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have…

blocks.text: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a years-long legal battle over their French winery, according to a joint statement from the former Hollywood couple.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives for Jolie and Pitt said in a statement. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”
Both sides have moved to dismiss claims against each other. The terms of the agreement were not made public.
The couple had bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008, and married there in 2014.

Jolie initiated divorce proceedings in 2016, and the couple was declared legally single in 2019, although their divorce settlement continued to play out until 2024. Jolie was cleared to sell her share in 2021 for $164m (£125.06m) before their wider financial settlement was finalized.

Pitt filed the lawsuit against Jolie in February 2022, after the actor sold her stake in the French winery to the Stoli Group, a spirits maker controlled by oligarch Yuri Shefler. In the suit, Pitt said Jolie had broken their agreement not to sell their interests in the winery without the other’s consent after she sold her stake to the Russian businessman.

In October 2022, Jolie filed a counter lawsuit against Pitt, which for the first time described alleged abusive behavior that led to their divorce. The actor’s attorneys said negotiations for Jolie to sell her share in the winery to Pitt broke down over his demand that she sign “a nondisclosure agreement that would have contractually prohibited her from speaking outside of court about Pitt’s physical and emotional abuse of her and their children”. Pitt denied the accusations.

articles.title: Senate committee recommends changing Liberals' data access bill following cybersecurity concerns
articles.summary: Senators on the national security committee want to see some changes made to a deeply divisive Liberal bill that would give police and intelligence agencies easier access to Canadians' private…

image.caption: A Senate committee is suggesting changes to a bill that deals with how organizations like the RCMP and CSIS can legally access Canadians' cellphone data for investigations. (Sean Kilpatrick/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Senators on the national security committee want to see some changes made to a deeply divisive Liberal bill that would give police and intelligence agencies easier access to Canadians' private information.
Amendment to change metadata retention provision fails
Over the past two days, the upper chamber's national security, defence and veterans affairs committee has been going through Bill C-22 clause by clause.
It agreed to further amend the landmark security bill.

The bill, known as lawful access legislation, would compel tech companies to adapt their systems to preserve data and then turn it over to law enforcement and the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) if they have a warrant.

The bill also gives the minister of public safety the authority to issue confidential orders to electronic service providers and forces them to retain user metadata — information that can include the sender, recipient and timing of communications — for up to six months.

It has pitted the government and security community — who argue the bill is essential for investigators to keep pace in a digital age — against privacy proponents, civil liberty advocates and some of the world's largest tech companies who have all raised concerns about opening up access to encrypted information.

items: Big tech, law enforcement make final pitches as Senate considers data access bill's future
Meta would 'consider' pulling services from Canada if lawful access bill passes as is

blocks.text: In the spring, Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree amended the bill to limit decryption requirements to when providers built the encryption and hold the keys necessary to unlock it. He clarified that companies don't have to comply with a ministerial order if doing so would require the company to introduce a "systemic vulnerability."
Industry continued to argue the bill would force force them introduce back doors, ultimately weakening their cyber defences.
On Tuesday night, the Senate committee supported amending the bill to further clarify the definition of "systemic vulnerability" to cover a credible risk that secure information could be accessed.
Another change made Wednesday would allow providers to request that the minister consult a new technical advisory committee about whether a directive would introduce a vulnerability.
The minister would also be able to proactively consult this advisory committee.
Bill still compels 6 months of metadata retention
The committee debated but ultimately did not make any substantial changes when it came to the bill's contentious provision requiring providers to hold on to metadata for six months.

Privacy advocates and businesses have been arguing that stockpiling months of metadata on millions of people even if they're not tied to a crime is an attractive target for foreign adversaries and hacking groups.

The head of the Toronto-based VPN provider Windscribe told the Senate committee earlier this week he will move his company out of Canada if this bill passes because he has made an explicit promise to users that his company doesn't store their information.

items: Ottawa makes $6B investment in Canada's spy agency over next decade

blocks.text: Nova Scotia Sen. Colin Deacon moved an amendment that would have prevented the government from compelling technology companies to retain metadata if they don't otherwise collect that type of data for business purposes, but it was defeated.

Senators will eventually vote on whether to approve the bill with amendments. It would then be sent back to the House of Commons, where the Liberals hold a majority, to decide whether to accept, reject or further amend the bill.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dead at 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died. He was 65.

image.caption: Andy Taylor of Duran Duran performs on stage in April 2004 during a celebration of the band's 25th anniversary. Taylor died this week at the age of 65, his family and bandmates said in a statement posted on social media Wednesday. (Jo Hale/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died. He was 65.
Taylor brought 'indelible fire and swagger to our music', band says in statement
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.
"From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," the band said.

"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed."
On the night he was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

items: Duran Duran still 'preaching to the unconverted' 38 years later

blocks.text: "I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
The band's huge pop hits include Hungry Like the Wolf, The Reflex and Rio and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV.

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the UK and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.
Andy Taylor, second from right, poses with his bandmates of British pop group Duran Duran in 1983. (Express Newspapers/Getty Images)
Fashion, synthesizers and glam-pop

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as Girls on Film and Union of the Snake and the moody ballads The Chauffeur and Save a Prayer. Other hits in the coming years included The Wild Boys, New Moon on Monday and Come Undone.
Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song A View to a Kill and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesizers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, which meant a lot to the band.
The band's success was in large part to their videos, including their Antigua-set song Rio, which featured shots of the band in pastel suits sailing confidently on a yacht.
From the archives: Duran Duran plays Calgary at the height of their fame

For the album Rio, they shot three music videos in Sri Lanka — including Save a Prayer, for which bass guitarist John Taylor was sprayed by an elephant — and two in Antigua, feeding MTV's need to have a stream of visuals, something classic rock didn't have.
"A lot of the success of the album is down to the power of the videos and the way it made the band omnipresent around the globe," Le Bon told the Daily Beast in 2012.
Andy Taylor agreed: "I don't think we could have done it without MTV."

articles.title: At least 30 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
articles.summary:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 25 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway…

blocks.text: A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the public prosecutor’s office said in a statement.
The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the health ministry.

blocks.caption: Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb, where charred vehicles remained after the blaze. Photograph: Amr Abdallah Dalsh/Reuters

blocks.text: At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.
The Egyptian president, Abdel-Fattah al-Sissi, expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The public prosecutor’s office said DNA investigations were under way to identify the victims.

The health minister, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic incidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

articles.title: At least 31 dead after fuel tanker fire in Egypt
articles.summary: Thirty-one people were killed and 21 wounded in a fire after a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned on a major ring road in Egypt, authorities said on Wednesday.

image.caption: A fire burning at the site where a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Egypt on Wednesday. (Habiba Abd El Aziz/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Thirty-one people were killed and 21 wounded in a fire after a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned on a major ring road in Egypt, authorities said on Wednesday.
More than 20 people also hurt after tanker truck carrying petroleum product overturns, health ministry says

The fire broke out above a tunnel in Giza's Al-Warraq district, the public prosecution said. Preliminary estimates found that 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, had been charred, it said, adding that casualty figures and damage were still being assessed.
The prosecution ordered DNA samples to be taken from the bodies of victims who had not yet been identified to establish their identities.
Thirty-nine ambulances took part in rescue operations, the health ministry said.
People look at the charred remains of a vehicle at the crash site. (Amr Abdallah Dalsh/Reuters)
Videos circulating on social media showed thick plumes of smoke billowing from the scene.

Reuters verified the location from the buildings and road layout, which matched archive and satellite imagery of the area. The date was confirmed through the original file's metadata. The date was also confirmed through local media reports and a statement from the health ministry.
"The cars were charred, with people inside them. They did not have time to get out," Ali Youssef, who was at the scene, said. "The fire burned the vehicles and the people inside."
Another burned vehicle at the crash site on Wednesday. (Amr Abdallah Dalsh/Reuters)

Reuters footage from the scene in Giza showed firefighting vehicles, charred cars and minibuses, burnt motorcycles and debris scattered across the major ring road, while people and security personnel inspected the aftermath and a bulldozer moved damaged vehicles.
The ring road connects key highways across Greater Cairo, linking the governorates of Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia.
Road accidents are common in Egypt due to factors including speeding, weak enforcement of traffic regulations and poor road conditions.

items: Death toll rises to 39 after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal
Tanker ship collides with riverboat carrying 129 people in New Orleans

blocks.text: The number of people killed in road accidents rose 10.8 per cent to 5,829 in 2025 from 5,260 a year earlier, according to the state statistics agency CAPMAS.

Egypt has expanded its road network in recent years, building highways and bridges under a broader infrastructure program aimed at easing congestion and accommodating rapid population growth and urban expansion. The projects have improved traffic flow in some areas, but concerns over road safety persist.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist in Duran Duran, dies aged 65
articles.summary:
Musician who had huge 1980s chart success had been diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2018

Andy Taylor, the guitarist with 80s pop megastars Duran Duran, has died aged 65.

He had been…

blocks.text: Andy Taylor, the guitarist with 80s pop megastars Duran Duran, has died aged 65.
He had been diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, which he disclosed publicly in 2022 when Duran Duran were about to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

“To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather,” read a statement shared with Variety. “He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.”

A statement from Duran Duran added: “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.”

Taylor was born in 1961 and grew up in Cullercoats, Northumberland, in a family who worked in the local fishing industry. He began playing guitar from the age of 11 and was tutored by Dave Black of the David Bowie backing band the Spiders from Mars. He left school early to start playing in bands on the working men’s club scene.

In 1980 he joined the nascent Duran Duran, who had formed in 1978 but whose lineup was far from settled – they advertised for a guitarist in Melody Maker, and Taylor travelled to Birmingham to audition. “A couple of days later they rang me and said out of 40 or so I was the only one who knew how to tune up, let alone play,” he later recalled.

The following month Simon Le Bon joined as frontman, by February 1981 they had released their debut single Planet Earth, and with the July release of Girls on Film – a song propelled by Taylor’s ultra-tight and rhythmic playing – they became major stars in the UK and US. Rio, their second album released in 1982, cemented their international playboy image and went Top 10 in both countries, and follow-up Seven and the Ragged Tiger topped the UK chart. Speaking to Smash Hits in 1983, Taylor described his new-found career as “a hobby gone mad”. That year Taylor also opened a wine bar called Rio, in Whitley Bay in his native Tyneside.

blocks.caption: Andy Taylor (centre) with Duran Duran in Japan in 1982. Photograph: Koh Hasebe/Shinko Music/Getty Images

blocks.text: Following their third album Duran Duran went on a brief hiatus, during which time Taylor and bassist John Taylor (no relation) formed a new funk-rock group, the Power Station, with singer Robert Palmer and former Chic drummer Tony Thompson. Two singles, the original track Some Like It Hot and a cover of T Rex’s Get It On, reached the US Top 10 in 1985.

Later that year Taylor rejoined Duran Duran to record A View to a Kill, the US chart-topping James Bond film theme, and perform with them at Live Aid in Philadelphia. But amid drug use, relations had become strained: drummer Roger Taylor left due to exhaustion, and Andy Taylor himself left to pursue the rockier direction he began with the Power Station – though his Duran Duran bandmates initially believed he would be continuing with the band.

“I’d come close to a nervous breakdown from the stresses of our crazy life and my own cocaine problem,” Taylor later said. “Combine that with all the shouting matches and the icy silences – I just knew I had to get out. So I did. The day after Live Aid, I stopped drinking and taking drugs. And I quietly started getting legal advice on extricating myself from Duran Duran.”

Collaborating with Sex Pistols’ Steve Jones, he released a solo LP, Thunder, in 1986, and the single Take It Easy was a minor US hit. As well as recording a covers album, Dangerous, he spent a number of years as a writer and producer for hire, with his song Lost in You becoming a transatlantic hit for Rod Stewart in 1988.

The Power Station briefly reunited in 1996, and then in 2000, the classic lineup of Duran Duran reformed and released a new album together, Astronaut, in 2004. He also toured with the band and worked on another (later scrapped) album Reportage, but was hit hard by the death of his father to cancer, and left the band again in 2006; he was diagnosed with depression the following year.

He spent the next decade away from music, first publishing his memoir Wild Boy: My Life in Duran Duran in 2008. He released a new solo single in 2019 and joined British rock band Reef as a tour guitarist, also producing their 2022 album Shoot Me Your Ace.

Despite the at-times fractious relationship with Duran Duran over the years, Taylor said in his statement accompanying the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction that there was no “bad blood … just pure love and respect for everything we wrote, recorded and achieved together”.
He married his wife Tracey Wilson in 1982, and they had four children together: Andrew, Georgina, Bethany and Isabella.

Following his cancer diagnosis, he credited his successful music career with keeping him upbeat. “I’ve been very fortunate, I’ve had so much, in terms of living the dream, but because I do music, I think that’s probably really helped me to live with pessimism of an incurable disease,” he said.

articles.title: Egypt: At least 31 dead after fuel truck overturns on highway
articles.summary: The accident occurred on the packed Ring Road in Giza near Cairo. Dozens of ambulances are responding to the crash, and Egyptian health authorities say the death toll could rise.

image.caption: Rescue workers rushed to the scene and pulled people out of burning cars Image: Mohammed Salah/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A fuel truck overturned on a packed highway in Giza, Egypt, on Wednesday, killing 31 people and injuring 21 more, according to Egyptian authorities.
What do we know so far?
The fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on Ring Road in Giza's Waraq district. The Ring Road encircles the greater Cairo metropolitan area.

Egyptian Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were transported to nearby hospitals and added that the death toll could rise further. He said 39 ambulances are responding to the accident.

blocks.caption: Cars were seen burned out after the accidentImage: Mahmoud el-Khawas/AFP

blocks.text: A massive fire broke out after the accident, with rescue workers pulling people from their vehicles. A large crowd gathered in the densely populated Waraq neighborhood amid the rescue efforts.
An investigation has been launched into the crash, according to Egypt's public prosecutor. DNA tests are being carried out to identify badly burned victims of the blaze.
El-Sissi expresses condolences to the victims

Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his deepest condolences and sympathy to the victims and directed relevant authorities to provide necessary support to the families of the victims and the injured.

Italian Foreign Affairs Minister Antonio Tajani said he extended his "deepest solidarity to the victims' families," Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty "and to the Egyptian people, whom I count as friends, at this tragic time."
Car accidents are frequent in Egypt due to poor road conditions, reckless driving and lax enforcement of safety rules.

articles.title: At least 30 killed in massive fire as fuel truck crashes on Cairo highway
articles.summary: Another 19 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

blocks.text: At least 30 people have been killed and 19 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.
Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.
Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the fuel truck had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.
The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.
It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.
Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

articles.title: Final Avengers: Doomsday trailer racks up over 500 million views in 1st day
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming Avengers movie, and it generated 563 million views in the first 24 hours. That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time,…

image.caption: Avengers: Doomsday hits theatres on Dec. 18. It will be the first Avengers film since Avengers: Endgame in 2019. (Marvel Studios)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

On Tuesday, Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming Avengers movie, and it generated 563 million views in the first 24 hours. That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time, beating out the previous Avengers: Doomsday teaser, which hit 503 million views in the first 24 hours.
While many fans are hyped, some have called out some of the trailer's visuals
It's safe to say there's a fair amount of hype around the upcoming release of Avengers: Doomsday.
Marvel released the final trailer for the upcoming superhero movie on Tuesday, and after just 24 hours it had already generated 563 million views.

That makes it the most viewed Disney trailer of all time, beating out the previous Avengers: Doomsday teaser, which hit 503 million views in the first 24 hours. It's also already the second most viewed movie trailer of all time, just below Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has over 718 million views.
The film, directed by Anthony Russo and Joe Russo — who also directed Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame — is set to hit theatres Dec. 18.

The trailer starts by showing Steve Rogers, played by Chris Evans, as he talks about fatherhood, and if he should tell his son about his past life as Captain America and an Avenger. He's then approached by Reed Richards, played by Pedro Pascal, and the rest of the Fantastic Four.
That's followed by a shot of Doctor Doom, played by Robert Downey Jr., accompanied by three mysterious masked women.

More heroes meet each other (and in some cases fight) including Canadian Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, Ian McKellen as Magneto and Chris Hemsworth as Thor. Though he doesn't appear in this trailer, Doomsday will be the final big-screen role for Patrick Stewart, who plays Charles Xavier, the leader of the X-Men.
Mixed reviews
"My family and I have booked the entire movie theatre for ourselves for the premiere of Avengers: Doomsday," posted X user @JesabelRaay. "They all couldn't stop talking about the new trailer."
But not all the hype is positive.
In the final scene, many of the heroes come together on a sort of battleground, and viewers weren't impressed.
"Avengers: Doomsday looks hideous … it visually looks awful," said @constantine_james7 in a video on Instagram.
Another Instagramer, @screened_scored, said it looked like "they took a bunch of individual characters, cut them out, and placed them against a digital background."
What is hype worth?

The last Avengers film, 2019's Avengers: Endgame, made $2.9 billion US at the box office (With a bump from the recently released slightly updated version) making it the highest-grossing movie of all time, not accounting for inflation.
But other recent films with high trailer views have done well.
While many fans are excited for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday movie, some took to social media to complain about some of the visuals in the latest trailer. (Marvel Studios)
The hype around Spider-Man: Brand New Day translated into box office success, with the movie pulling in $2.52 billion US worldwide
Deadpool & Wolverine's 2024 Super Bowl teaser scored 365 million views if you include those who watched the trailer during the Super Bowl broadcast, and that movie took in $1.3 billion US globally.
Possible hidden secrets
Keen-eyed viewers believe they aren't exactly seeing everything in these trailers.

At the end of the recent release, many of the heroes team up for a classic "Avengers, assemble" shot that often accompanies these big team-up movies when all the heroes unite to fight against common enemy.
But some viewers have pointed out that there are some gaps where they believe characters have been digitally edited out.
While much of the cast has been announced, there are still some unknowns around who will appear in the movie, such as three characters pictured here. (Marvel Studios)
It wouldn't be the first time.

In a trailer for Spider-Man: No Way Home, Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield playing their versions of Spider-Man were edited out of the trailer that otherwise would've shown them swinging into action with Tom Holland's Spider-Man.
In trailers for Endgame, Thor and Bruce Banner's Smart Hulk were edited out of scenes, so it wouldn't give away their appearance.
Tickets for the Dec. 18 release of Avengers: Doomsday have been on sale since July. It will premier the same day as Dune: Part Three directed by Canadian Denis Villeneuve.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Philip Drost is a network senior writer for CBC News based in Fredericton. You can reach him at philip.drost@cbc.ca.

articles.title: New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade postponed due to weather
articles.summary:
Forecasters say high winds on Thursday may spoil the annual march of huge balloons and have moved the parade to Saturday

New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed due…

blocks.text: New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed due to excessively windy weather and will now be held on Saturday.

Forecasters say an impending storm on Thursday may spoil the street party, which is marked by a march of huge balloons. AccuWeather is forecasting winds of 12 to 25 mph (19 to 40 km/h) and rain later on Thursday.
Under guidelines, large balloons must stay grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph (37 km/h) or gusts exceed 34 mph (55 km/h). The parade balloons have been grounded only once previously, in 1971.
NBC quoted Macy’s as saying: “The safety of our participants and spectators is our priority.”
Macy’s added: “Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

This year the parade will include a tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty, and special appearances by Melissa Joan Hart, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer and Holly Robinson Peete, all leading the way for Santa Claus. Nine Broadway shows will be featured as part of a 10-minute medley, replacing the traditional sprinkling of full show numbers.

The Macy’s parade began more than a century ago in 1924 as a way of creating buzz for the giant department store’s holiday windows at Macy’s Herald Square flagship store in Manhattan. Macy’s borrowed animals from the Central Park Zoo for the first parades but in 1927 ended that practice after children were getting scared.

The animals were then replaced with air-filled balloons and, a year later, balloons that could be filled with helium – a now familiar sight for people around the world from countless Hollywood movies set in New York City.

The parades have been fully cancelled previously only in 1942, 1943 and 1944 because the valuable materials needed to create the huge balloons were diverted for the the second world war effort against Germany and Japan.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: B.C.'s new premier outlines 3 immediate priorities after first cabinet meeting
articles.summary: B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson says he's taking immediate action on three top priorities after his first cabinet meeting. They include posting a notice of intent for a design of a bridge option to…

image.caption: B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson speaks at a news conference on Wednesday. (Mike McArthur/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia

B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson says he's taking immediate action on three top priorities after his first cabinet meeting. They include posting a notice of intent for a design of a bridge option to replace the George Massey Tunnel, taking SOGI 123 materials off government websites, and starting a return-to-office plan for the B.C. Public Service.
Lorne Doerkson's top 3 to-dos: George Massey replacement, removing SOGI materials, return-to-office
B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson has announced he's taking immediate action on three top priorities after his first cabinet meeting.
Doerkson listed his first priority as posting a notice of intent for a design of a bridge option to replace the George Massey Tunnel between Richmond and Delta.
He said at a news conference Wednesday afternoon the notice would be posted later in the day and will ask the current contractor to do the work.
He said cabinet would review the numbers before making a final decision to ensure the project is the most cost-effective.
"Our responsibility is to ensure taxpayers get the best value for their money," Doerkson said.
He said British Columbians want access over the river, and he wants the space to understand the project.
"I am, obviously, very big on 'bridge' right now, but I do want to understand a few things just before that final decision happens, and I hope that to happen before Christmas."
The previous B.C. NDP government had planned to replace the tunnel, rather than build a bridge.

items: Here are 5 promises the B.C. Conservative government could get started on right away
B.C. Premier Doerkson's mandate letters call for health-care guarantee, reforming carbon pricing

blocks.text: Secondly, Doerkson said SOGI 123 materials will be taken off government websites "as of today."

SOGI (which stands for sexual orientation and gender identity) 123 has been a resource teachers and educators can turn to to make schools safer and more inclusive for students of all gender identities and orientations, according to its website.
Doerkson said the Ministry of Education will work with school districts to take SOGI 123 materials out of schools.
"We are starting that work right now."
He said parents should have a say in how and when "sensitive topics" are introduced in schools.
"We want our schools to be safe and welcoming places, of course, for every student, with a strong focus on reading, writing, arithmetic and on teaching kids to think for themselves," Doerkson said.

items: Can the B.C. Conservatives actually repeal SOGI 123 in schools? What you need to know

blocks.text: He said he wants to "better understand how our schools were not safe prior to SOGI" and "how we will make sure that our student body is safe."
He added: "SOGI, of course, has been conflated with so much now — I'm not certain that I've even been able to get a good explanation from ministry staff or from teachers, frankly, on this topic."
Doerkson responded to a reporter's question on what would happen if teachers continue to use the SOGI resource.
"We've asked for it to be removed from the rooms, so it's not just that they'll get pushback from parents, but they'll get pushback from me as well."
Return-to-office planned for public servants
Doerkson's third priority is for B.C. Public Service workers to return to the office in a phased plan.
Those who can work from the office "will be back at it, five days a week," Doerkson said.
He said he's written to the head of the public service to start planning for the return-to-office policy.
He said thousands of public servants, such as nurses, teachers, correctional workers and those providing frontline services, have never had the choice to work remotely.
"I think it's reasonable to ask for people in our offices to do the same," Doerkson said, adding people collaborate better in the same room.
With files from Akshay Kulkarni

articles.title: Buster the hamster home safe after hitching ride in Halloween pumpkin
articles.summary: A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.

image.caption: Covered in orange pumpkin juice, one family’s pet hamster, Buster, turned up inside a donated pumpkin that was left for over 21 days. (Castlegarth Farms/Facebook)

blocks.text: Ottawa·New
A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.
Couple found Arnprior family's pet on their farm 3 weeks later and 20 km away
· CBC News
· Posted: Nov 25, 2026 3:39 PM EST | Last Updated: 8 minutes ago
Every November, Matthew Brearley and Tanya Sprowl collect donated pumpkins at Castlegarth Farms in White Lake, Ont., where they're used for compost.
The couple told CBC’s Ottawa Morning that they typically inspect the pumpkins for non-compostable items such as forgotten tea lights.

"We go through each pumpkin, piling it on the compost pile, and there was quite a sizable amount," Brearly said. "I was turning it over, looked down and saw what I thought was not a hamster, but [another kind of] small rodent, which does happen on farms."
But after a closer look, Brearley realized this was no typical farmyard rodent, but a domesticated hamster that's definitely not native to the Ottawa Valley.
Buster had spent an estimated 21 days inside the pumpkin, where he at least had plenty to eat.
"He was quite wet, he was covered in pumpkin guts and juice," said Sprowl. "So he was a little scraggly, but he seemed otherwise OK and didn’t have any injuries."
'That's Buster!'

Brearley scooped the hamster up and brought him into the house to be properly fed and cleaned. Figuring he was someone's missing pet, the couple took Buster's "mug shot" and posted it to a local Facebook group in an attempt to find his owners.

"He must have crawled into one of their Halloween pumpkins to have a snack and then ended up in the pile at the Nick Smith Centre bound for a dump truck that was headed to our farm for composting," the Facebook post read.
Word spread quickly.
"People followed the story all weekend looking for updates. It was kind of funny,” Brearley said.
Eventually, a family from Arnprior reached out.
"They sent us a direct message saying, 'That’s Buster!’ and they had been tearing their house apart for the last three weeks looking for their hamster," Sprowl said.
Sprowl said Buster was finally reunited with his owners after being "fluffed up" and made more presentable. Buster's family, which includes three boys, declined to comment for this story.
Brearley said it was an unexpectedly happy ending to a remarkable adventure.
"I would’ve been surprised if my hamster disappeared three weeks ago. I would’ve assumed it gone forever, but there it was, no foul and reunited with its family,” he said.
"He’s one lucky hamster that’s for sure,” the couple wrote on Facebook, thanking the online community for helping make Buster's homecoming happen.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Cassandra Bellefeuille is a journalist with CBC Ottawa. She covers municipal affairs, politics and local news. She holds a combined honours degree in journalism and political science from Carleton University.

articles.title: PQ urges other parties urged to sit in Quebec legislature — despite recent ruling ordering oath to King
articles.summary: The battle over whether Quebec legislators will have to swear an oath to the King continues, with an appeal hearing scheduled for Friday. The premier wants his opponents to join him in sitting in the…

image.caption: Parti Québécois House leader Catherine Gentilcore (left) and Quebec's minister of justice, Marie-Claude Sarrazin (right), confirmed at the National Assembly on Wednesday that their party was ready to sit as planned next Tuesday, regardless of the outcome of ongoing legal proceedings relating to legi

blocks.text: Montreal·New

The battle over whether Quebec legislators will have to swear an oath to the King continues, with an appeal hearing scheduled for Friday. The premier wants his opponents to join him in sitting in the legislative session, regardless of the outcome of the court ruling.
Superior Court ruling suspended law that made oath optional; appeal to be heard Friday

Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is encouraging his opponents to join him in taking their seats at the National Assembly next Tuesday, despite a Quebec Superior Court judge’s ruling ordering legislators to swear allegiance to the King before sitting at the National Assembly.
Justice Ian Demers warned on Monday that laws passed at the National Assembly could be rendered invalid if members do not take the oath.
The government is contesting the decision. The appeal will be heard at 2 p.m. on Friday in Montreal.
"We believe that, in any case, there is absolutely nothing preventing us from sitting," said Parti Québécois (PQ) parliamentary leader Catherine Gentilcore on Wednesday.

Even though the appeal has not yet been heard, the premier has sent a letter to the leaders of the three opposition parties, urging them to commit "to begin our parliamentary work on December 1, with our oaths as they currently stand."
During the swearing-in ceremonies of each party, the MNAs made their oaths to the Quebec people. It was Bill 4, passed unanimously in Quebec in Dec. 2022, that made the oath to the Crown optional.

Demers said in his Monday ruling, though, that the Quebec government had overstepped its constitutional boundaries with this law. He wrote that "the Constitution is not an à la carte menu" from which individuals can pick and choose what to follow.

items: Quebec's legislative session in limbo as court mandates oath to the King
Could the Parti Québécois actually abolish the monarchy in Quebec?

blocks.text: All the parties have said they want the legislative session to start next Tuesday as planned. However, they've expressed varying degrees of resistance to pledging allegiance to King Charles.
Quebec Liberal Leader Charles Milliard has said he won't rule out taking the oath.
"It wouldn't be responsible to close any doors except the one that we will not be postponing the session," he said on Tuesday.
Quebec Conservative Party Leader Éric Duhaime has voiced support for protecting the parliamentary sovereignty of the National Assembly, while also showing a willingness to be flexible.
"It's not because you know you're saying those words before you're getting into the House that necessarily you become a federalist and a monarchist," Duhaime said.

items: Lieutenant-governor will skip Quebec cabinet's swearing-in at incoming premier's request

blocks.text: Meanwhile, the province's political parties have reached an agreement to change another National Assembly rule.

When the premier marks the opening of the legislative session, the new Speaker of the National Assembly will table the written speech of the lieutenant-governor, who's a representative of the monarchy.
The lieutenant-governor has traditionally delivered an opening address at the start of a new legislative session.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Patricia Kozicka is a digital journalist with CBC Montreal. She has previously worked in Toronto and Edmonton. You can reach her at patricia.kozicka@cbc.ca.
With files from CBC's Cathy Senay, Benjamin Shingler and Radio-Canada's Jérôme Labbé

articles.title: Nigeria detains 5 Mexicans, confiscates over $220 million of meth
articles.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern state of Enugu.

image.caption: At least 10 Mexicans are now in Nigerian custody, including five from an earlier raidImage: NDLEA/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLA) said Wednesday it had arrested five Mexicans and confiscated over $220 million (around €200 million) in methamphetamine as part of a significant drug bust.
What do we know about the drug bust?
The agency said the Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern Nigerian state of Enugu.

"A total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of $226.8 million was recovered from the clandestine factory," NDLA spokesperson Femi Babafemi said.

Nigeria first rejected the entry of the Mexicans into the country in August. They later entered Nigeria again in September via neighboring Benin using forged passports, with authorities then putting them under surveillance.
On November 11, the Mexicans were taken into custody at the Enugu lab after their movements were tracked by the Nigerian government. A Nigerian was also arrested in a nearby hotel.

blocks.caption: Nigerian authorities inspected the Enugu facility and seized industrial equipment along with chemicalsImage: NDLEA/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: The latest drug bust comes after Nigerian authorities in May also detained 10 people in a anti-meth operation in the southwest, including three Mexicans.
Why do Mexican cartels find African countries desirable for drug production?

The arrests raise concern that Mexican cartels are getting a foothold in Africa for international drug trafficking. In addition to Nigeria, South Africa is another country where Mexicans have been arrested for being involved in a meth lab.

According to Vanda Felbab-Brown, an expert at the Washington DC-based Brookings Institution, Mexican cartels such as the Sinaloa Cartel and the Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generation (CJNG) have expanded their operations into other continents such as Africa.
How drug cartels expand their reach across West Africa

In a June testimony to the US Senate Caucus on International Narcotics Control, Felbab-Brown said the cartels find "desirable partners" for production in countries such as South Africa and Kenya due to factors such as "limited law enforcement capacities and entrenched criminal and corrupt networks."
According to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime,criminal networks often take advantage of porous borders in the West and Central Africa region to carry out activities such as illicit drug trafficking.

"Many countries in the region have vast territory and borders are located either in very remote or densely populated areas, thus making law enforcement activities particularly difficult to conduct in an efficient manner," the office said. "The porous nature of the borders in West and Central Africa is a major factor of insecurity: the borders are neither demarcated or sufficiently controlled."

articles.title: Australian politics live: federal Liberal senator Leah Blyth defects to One Nation
articles.summary: • Get our breaking news email, free app or

blocks.text: Federal Liberal senator Leah Blyth defects to One Nation
Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, is defecting to One Nation and will become the party’s first upper-house member for the state, according to The Australian.
The move will cause recriminations in Coalition ranks because Blyth is a member of Angus Taylor’s shadow cabinet.
But she told the paper she no longer felt the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government, which was “running the country into the ground”.
She said:

double quotation markI can no longer in good conscience tell Australians that the Liberal party can save this country. Australia is a country worth fighting for … I want our children to grow up proud of their country, with the freedom and opportunity to build a better life. One Nation has never shied away from confronting the uncomfortable truths facing our nation. They are the only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around.
Key events

items: 12m agoBlyth ‘wasn’t a big contributor to the party room’: Jane Hume
31m agoBlyth defection ‘smacks of self-interest’, Nationals leader says
44m agoFederal Liberal senator Leah Blyth defects to One Nation
46m agoEnergy minister says geopolitical tension ‘infected’ Cop31 talks

blocks.text: Blyth defection shows disunity in Liberal party: Cabinet minister

Labor will get a good kick out of this story today, particularly after securing a few legislative wins with the help of the Greens this week. (Although I would say the wins were bigger for the Greens who got massive concessions out of the government on the digital duty of care, trusts, and private health insurance bills.)
Cabinet minister, Pat Conroy, doesn’t want to stick the knife in too hard though this morning, deferring the question to the Coalition.
But he says regardless of who defects where, the Liberals and One Nation “can’t govern without each other”.
He tells ABC News Breakfast:

double quotation markWe are facing at the next election clearly a Coalition and Liberals and One Nation with all the baggage that each of these parties brings to the table. They’re all anti-worker, they’re all extreme … this demonstrates, I think, more disunity in the Liberal Party under Angus Taylor.
Blyth ‘wasn’t a big contributor to the party room’: Jane Hume
The claws are OUT this morning.
The deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume, has been stopped by journos on her way into Parliament House, and is clearly incensed by her Senate colleague Leah Blyth’s defection.
She, like Matt Canavan, says it’s a “disappointing decision”.

double quotation markThe fact that she feels that the Liberal party doesn’t reflect her views any more is a surprise to all of us. It’s certainly not something that she ever mentioned in the party room – but she wasn’t a big contributor to the party room.
Ouch.
Asked what her highlight of the year is, Hume says “unity” in the Liberal and National parties (notwithstanding the last 24 hours).

blocks.caption: Jane Hume in the Coalition party room on Tuesday. Photograph: Hilary Wardhaugh/Getty Images

blocks.text: ‘Turncoat town’: Canavan takes a crack at Blyth and One Nation
Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, is pretty salty this morning – taking another crack at Leah Blyth over her defection from the Liberal party to One Nation.
He calls One Nation “turncoat town” by hoovering up defectors from other parties.
Speaking to journos in the press gallery corridor after his RN Breakfast interview, he doesn’t hold back:

double quotation markI think people see that as a defection, as a turncoat, and One Nation is becoming turncoat town right now, where they seem to be much more focused on taking people away from other political parties than changing the government, and therefore changing the policy and changing the direction of this country. I don’t buy Leah’s explanation that this is some grand policy principle. It instead just smacks of self-interest.

blocks.caption: Krishani Dhanji

blocks.text: Krishani Dhanji
Good morning
Krishani Dhanji here with you for the final sitting day of the year, thanks to Martin Farrer.
Just when I thought this week couldn’t get any busier, Leah Blyth said “hold my beer”.
It’s going to be a cracker today – let’s get stuck in!
Blyth defection ‘smacks of self-interest’, Nationals leader says
The Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, has called Leah Blyth’s defection to One Nation “disappointing on a number of levels”.
Speaking to Radio National, Canavan said he thought he was friends with Blyth but that he had received no warning of her move.

double quotation markI always find it disappointing when someone leaves the party [that] they were elected under, particularly in the Senate, because I know as a senator, you’re not really elected in your own name, you’re elected as a party … And so it’s right that people feel a bit let down when someone[who is] elected by them ticking a party box changes parties after the election.
Speaking to Blyth’s reasoning that her values aligned more closely with One Nation, Canavan said the move “smacks of self-interest to me”.

double quotation markGood luck to her. Leah went to the election last year supporting net zero. She didn’t oppose the hate speech laws earlier this year, like we did – the Nationals. To turn around now a few months later and say … “my principles and policies are more aligned with One Nation,” I mean, give me a break.

blocks.caption: Matt Canavan. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP

blocks.text: Energy minister says geopolitical tension ‘infected’ Cop31 talks

blocks.caption: Catie McLeod

blocks.text: Catie McLeod
The energy minister, Chris Bowen, has said the failed Cop31 negotiations he presided over were more strained than previous years.

Bowen, who served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkey, was interviewed on the ABC’s 7.30 program last night about the conference, which did not result in consensus among the countries over a proposed “cover decision”, or an overarching agreement, for the conference.
Bowen told the ABC it was not unusual that the negotiations were difficult, but:

double quotation markThe difference this year was countries were a lot harder to budge from their position and frankly I felt a lot of geopolitical tension in the room on other issues infecting the conversation and making it so much harder to negotiate. I’ve been to five Cops, seen plenty of argy-bargy, but there was a lot more rigidness to the negotiations this year. We [Australia] have always supported transition away from fossil fuels. This year I had a slightly different job. Normally we go – I go – to Cops and argue for what should be in. This year my job, running the negotiation – was to find ... the strongest outcome that I could get 195 countries from Tuvalu to Saudi Arabia to agree [on].
As Guardian Australia previously reported, the biggest sticking point was whether the agreement would mention the need for the world to transition away from fossil fuels.

blocks.caption: Tess Ikonomou

blocks.text: Tess Ikonomou
Labor and Coalition on cusp of gas deal
A federal scheme requiring Australia’s largest gas exporters to keep up to a fifth of their product for domestic use is likely to be announced, with Labor and the Coalition on the cusp of a deal.
The Albanese government and the opposition have been locked in negotiations to reach an agreement before parliament breaks for the year after Thursday.
Labor agreed to a carve-out from the policy for Western Australia, as the mining state already has its own reservation scheme.
But the Coalition has held out over a provision that will require gas companies to oversupply the market by 10%, arguing it will affect future investment.
The opposition has remained the government’s partner of choice for this policy, as the Greens demanded a 25% tax on gas exports in return for their support.
Welcome
Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it will be Krishani Dhanji with the main action.

articles.title: Moment Nasa spacecraft hit asteroid - and what happened next
articles.summary: The crash was 'like something out of a disaster movie,' the BBC's science editor Rebecca Morelle says.

blocks.text: The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.
Video released by Nasa showed the moment of impact in 2022, while new images show the extent of the damage done to the asteroid.
Dimorphos, the asteroid, posed no threat to Earth, but the crash was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.
Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.
The BBC's science editor Rebecca Morelle explains.

articles.title: Oregon man and dog narrowly escape being swept away by high tides as officials urge caution at beaches
articles.summary:
Record-breaking king tides have prompted west coast authorities to warn residents to stay away from beaches

The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have…

blocks.text: The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have urged residents to avoid beaches, but not everyone is heeding those warnings.

In Cannon Beach, Oregon, viral footage showed a man and his dog nearly getting swept away by a so-called king tide on Tuesday morning. The man had been standing on a staircase holding his leashed dog, who was walking in the sand, when the water suddenly surged, knocking him to his feet.

They ultimately escaped without injury, according to the Cannon Beach police department. Earlier that morning, police had cited the same man for driving on the shoreline. He had reportedly “indicated” to an officer he wanted to get a better look at the high tides.
Other footage captured around Cannon Beach on Tuesday morning showed a jogger narrowly avoiding a major wave, while another stood amid the wave seemingly filming.

King tides are the highest tide cycles of the year. This winter, conditions caused by the super El Niño have pushed these tides to record levels, contributing to widespread flooding, powerful waves and coastal erosion.
The Cannon Beach police department advised residents to stay off beaches and keep pets away from the water.

“King tides are an impressive natural phenomenon, but no photograph, video or closer look is worth risking your life, the life of your pet or the lives of the first responders who may be called upon to rescue you,” the police department said in a statement.

A coastal flood advisory is in effect for the region through Thursday, according to the National Weather Service, as “king tides, elevated seas, and the arrival of fresh swells likely lead to tidal overflow”.

articles.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
articles.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in

blocks.text: The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Wilson’s talk on 23 November, titled “Little Black Stretchy Pants” after his memoir, was billed as an “intimate, fireside chat” offering insight into the “mind and instincts of the man himself”. It was moderated by Nuvyn Peters, CEO of Axis Connects.

There is no publicly available video of the event, but the Guardian spoke with people who attended it and reviewed social media posts from those present. Outrage over the event was first reported by the Globe and Mail.

According to people who were there, Wilson told the audience that companies would be reluctant to hire a 22-year-old woman because she might become pregnant at 23 and take maternity leave. He went on to suggest that women were waiting too long to have children, prompting men to import brides from Thailand.
“There were audible gasps in the room and everyone was clearly uncomfortable. It was a mix of disengaging, walking out and also just complete shock of what was being said on stage,” one person said.

“I am floored that Axis gave this man a platform. We all were saying before the event it was surprising he was there – and it’s clear that [Wilson] runs in the organizer’s circles after she opened with the fact that they go on walks [at a Vancouver mountain] together.”
The event, which was supposed to run for an hour, was cut short at 45 minutes.

The remarks are not the first time Wilson has attracted criticism for his comments about women and their bodies. He stepped down as chair of Lululemon’s board in 2013 after the company’s signature black yoga pants were criticized for being see-through and Wilson blamed the problem on the body types of some customers.
On Monday, he reportedly told the group that those prior comments about body types had been “misconstrued” and said he was referring to women who wear sizes that are too small.
Wilson, who is believed to be worth more than C$6bn, has not had a leadership role at Lululemon for several years but remains a major shareholder.
He also reportedly told the audience that poverty had largely been eradicated, and that he was looking forward to going to space with Elon Musk.

Audience members also said Wilson suggested that men were better suited to helm clothing companies that catered to women, because they knew what looked good on women’s bodies. He said the same was true of women who lead companies focused on men’s fashion.

“We recognize that several comments made by Chip Wilson at the Leadership Forum were offensive and inconsistent with the values and mission of Axis Connects,” Peters said in a statement. “We understand why those remarks caused concern and disappointment among members of our community. His comments also underscore an uncomfortable reality: attitudes and assumptions that hold women back in the workplace and in leadership have not disappeared. Challenging those attitudes is central to the work and ethos of Axis Connects.”

Wilson’s spokesperson pointed to the work the Lululemon founder has done to mentor and “empower” women in leadership roles over the years and said his efforts “speak for themselves”. A number of women who were early employees of the company and worked closely with Wilson became millionaires when the company went public, he has previously noted in his memoir, and have gone on to found their own businesses.

More than 700 women attended the conference, many representing organizations they worked for. One person said the experience left her “irate”, adding that it was also indicative of what women continued to tolerate.
“It’s just sad that this is what women still have to deal with, in a forum literally for women.”

articles.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
articles.summary: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

blocks.text: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.
They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.
Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".
"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.
"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."
Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.
In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.
"The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media report.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.
However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.
Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.
It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial.
He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.

The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.
The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.
For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.

This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.

While Netanyahu's parliamentary bloc won more seats than that of his rival, both fell short of an outright majority. Israel's president has offered Eisenkot the first chance to form a new administration.
Netanyahu remains subject to an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which he also denies.

articles.title: Health Canada issues warning on rare risk of vision loss with semaglutide GLP-1 drugs
articles.summary: A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.

image.caption: Health Canada has issued a public warning about the 'very rare but serious' risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs. (CBC)

blocks.text: Health·Breaking
A safety review from Health Canada has found a possible link between semaglutide GLP-1 drugs and a rare form of vision loss.
Federal team's safety review found possible link between use of drugs and 'very rare' eye condition
Health Canada has issued a public warning about the "very rare but serious" risk of vision loss tied to semaglutide GLP-1 drugs, known by brand names such as Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy.

On the heels of similar warnings in the U.S. and Europe, the federal department announced on Wednesday that it had completed its own safety review which found a possible link between prescription semaglutide drugs and the risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).
Described by Health Canada as "very rare," the eye condition causes sudden, painless blindness or vision changes due to reduced blood flow to the optic nerve.
The condition has no known treatment.
More to come.
